clue.text: Obtain timber of the same colour, which easily splinters

definitions.text: Obtain timber of the same colour
definitions.meaning: to get wood that matches in colour is, read as a verb phrase
wood that breaks into tiny fragments is fit only for kindling, as brittle as a struck stick

explanation.surface: A carpenter buys matching planks, only to find they shatter at the first nail.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchwood is wood reduced to small splinters, so it describes timber that breaks up readily.

clue.text: Declines to set sail

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are set out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone refuses an invitation to go sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declines' looks like 'refuses', but here it means 'grows weaker', and 'set' rearranges SAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline in health is to be unwell, a synonym for being poorly.

clue.text: Stripe no longer displayed by one stripped for corporal punishment

definitions.text: Stripe no longer displayed by one stripped for corporal punishment

parts.words: Stripe no longer displayed by one stripped for corporal punishment
parts.note: a corporal who is demoted ('stripped') as punishment loses the V-shaped rank badge on his sleeve; 'corporal punishment' puns on the rank

explanation.surface: A man is stripped to be flogged, his back no longer showing marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporal punishment' suggests flogging, but the punishment is of a corporal, who loses his rank badge.
explanation.definitionFit: The V-shaped sleeve badge worn by NCOs is a stripe; a demoted corporal loses it.

clue.text: Fish plate cleaning substance

definitions.meaning: a sea fish of the cod family
powdered chalk used to polish silver plate

explanation.surface: A kitchen hint about the stuff that cleans plates after a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a cod-like sea fish and the ground chalk used for polishing silverware.

clue.text: Fragments of a sort

indicators.note: 'of a sort' suggests the word sort in a loose, approximate form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bits and pieces of something, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' makes the following word only loosely itself: rearrange SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are scraps or leftovers of food, so they are fragments.

clue.text: Enjoy complete success with a broom on a bare floor

definitions.meaning: to win every prize or trick on offer

definitions.text: with a broom on a bare floor
definitions.meaning: literally, to brush the floorboards

explanation.surface: A cleaner triumphs at sweeping an uncarpeted room.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for winning everything comes from gathering all the stakes off the gaming table; literally it is brushing the floorboards.

clue.text: The drilling rig is now properly adjusted and running smoothly

definitions.meaning: an oil or water borehole that has been brought under control is a regulated well
in good order, like a smooth machine

explanation.surface: An engineer reports that the drilling rig is working nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something properly adjusted and orderly is described as functioning under good control; read literally, a borehole is under control.

clue.text: When King John woke up quarter of an hour after mid, night

definitions.text: When King John woke up quarter of an hour after mid, night

parts.words: When King John woke up quarter of an hour after mid, night
parts.note: midnight is the hour of twelve, and a quarter of an hour later is the time given; the comma splitting 'mid, night' teases a reading of Twelfth Night, another Shakespeare title beside King John

explanation.surface: A historical anecdote about the king stirring shortly after midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shakespeare titles King John and Twelfth Night hover over the clue, but it simply asks for a clock time just after midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter of an hour after midnight is the clock time written 12.15.

clue.text: Ordinary soldier has hesitation at becoming a pirate

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A humble soldier dithers before turning buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was an armed private ship or captain licensed to raid enemy shipping, a legalised pirate.

clue.text: Only part of the brew-house not yet crowded?

definitions.meaning: a room where distilling is done, in a great house where cordials were brewed
there is space left for more people

explanation.surface: Just one corner of the brewery has space left.
explanation.definitionFit: A still-room is the household room for distilling and preserves; read as two words it says space remains.

clue.text: Wind up drunk apparently

definitions.meaning: to wind in a line on a spool
to stagger as a drunk seems to

explanation.surface: Someone is getting irritated by an apparently tipsy companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both winding a fishing line onto a drum and lurching unsteadily.

clue.text: Noise abroad sounds like a beast

indicators.note: the clue tells us the answer is said the same as a word for a beast

parts.note: a brute is a savage animal

explanation.surface: An overseas racket resembles the roar of some animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noise abroad' is an old verb phrase meaning to spread a rumour, not a racket heard overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To bruit something is to spread it as rumour, to noise it abroad.

clue.text: About all that can happen to sour cream

definitions.text: that can happen to sour cream

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
the lot means everything

explanation.surface: A summary of everything that might befall cream once it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Soured cream curdles and thickens into lumps, which is to coagulate.

clue.text: Abusive name Caesar applied to an assassin

definitions.meaning: an insult calling someone a savage
Caesar's dying words 'Et tu, ...?' address Brutus by the Latin vocative of his name

explanation.surface: A history lesson on what Caesar called one of his murderers.
explanation.definitionFit: The insult for a savage person is also the Latin vocative of Brutus that Caesar uttered.

clue.text: Painful cross

definitions.meaning: inflamed and sore, as of a wound
annoyed

explanation.surface: Being annoyed hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both an inflamed, sore wound and an irritated temper.

clue.text: T.A. never resorts to one who could teach it a thing or two

definitions.text: one who could teach it a thing or two

indicators.note: read as re-sorts, the letters are sorted again into a new order

parts.note: T.A. is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: The Territorial Army never calls on an old hand who knows more than they do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorts' looks like 'turns to', but read as 're-sorts' it rearranges TA NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old soldier with long experience could instruct raw volunteers.

clue.text: Polite male, but a slippery one

parts.note: a gent is a man
an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: A man seems courteous but is untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means refined and well-mannered.

clue.text: Where the stage is set for an operation

definitions.meaning: a playhouse with its stage
an operating room in a hospital

explanation.surface: Preparations are in place for a planned operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a playhouse and a hospital operating room.

clue.text: 21:1 on are the odds in favour of its being caused by over cultivation

definitions.text: its being caused by over cultivation

parts.note: the answer to 21 across is the god of love
the numeral one looks like I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's odds that too much farming is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: '21:1 on' looks like betting odds, but 21 is a cross-reference to the god of love, and 1 is the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil worn away by overfarming is the classic case of land being worn down by wind and rain.

clue.text: Head steward accommodates socially acceptable follower

indicators.note: one word takes in the other, as a host takes in a guest

parts.note: the purser is the senior officer in charge of a ship's stewards
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A ship's chief steward takes on a well-bred hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuer is one who follows or chases another.

clue.text: Better cavalryman

definitions.meaning: one who bets, especially heavily and recklessly
old army slang for a horse soldier

explanation.surface: A superior horse soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless gambler and a cavalry soldier were both known by this slang term.

clue.text: Maybe standing on one foot in Piccadilly makes his back sore

definitions.text: Maybe standing on one foot in Piccadilly

indicators.note: the word that follows is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Standing on one leg in central London leaves a man aching.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue at Piccadilly Circus, a London landmark, is popularly called the god of love and is poised on one foot; 'back' turns SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged statue at Piccadilly Circus is popularly named for the god of love.

clue.text: Extra pay for getting on in public transport

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A worker earns more for boarding the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an additional payment over basic wages.

clue.text: Father needs nothing but skirting

parts.note: dad is father
O is the zero sign for nothing

explanation.surface: Dad wants nothing except to fit the skirting board.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower part of a room's wall, often a decorative skirting band.

clue.text: Foreign coin preferable to a cheque?

definitions.meaning: a small coin of China and the East
ready money, which a seller may prefer to a cheque

explanation.surface: Payment in foreign currency may be better than a cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a small Chinese coin is also the word for ready money.

clue.text: Short cuts to cuemanship practice?

parts.note: cuemanship sounds like the craft of the queue, an old word for a pigtail; short haircuts are a way of dispensing with it

explanation.surface: Quick routes to improving one's snooker technique.
explanation.walkthrough: The snooker cue misleads; a queue is a pigtail, and cropped hairstyles cut it away.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobs are short haircuts, cut level around the head.

clue.text: Getting out of a hiding for ruining the book-binding

definitions.meaning: emerging from a hiding place, as game does
literally damaging the cover of a book

explanation.surface: Escaping a beating for damaging a book's binding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an animal leaving shelter and, literally, splitting a book's cover.

clue.text: Bloomer led to an upper-cut taking effect

parts.note: an uppercut is a punch aimed at the chin, so the target stands for the blow
if one thing led to another, the second arose from it

explanation.surface: A gaffe sparked a punch that landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The China rose is a flowering shrub, a plant that blooms.
